title: Magnets pull strongly on iron and do not pull on copper
summary: NASA's intermediate note says iron is strongly attracted by magnets, and copper is not.
body: NASA's heliophysics learning page, in the intermediate wording on magnetic fields, says some materials such as iron are strongly attracted by magnets while other materials such as copper are not. The same page's introductory lines say that things made of metal, or other magnets, feel a pull or a push near a magnet. That introductory wording is broader than the intermediate sentence. This card follows the intermediate sentence, which separates iron from copper, and does not treat every metal as magnetic. OpenStax names a longer ferromagnetic list, including nickel and cobalt, on its own page. Those extra names are not added here.

sources.title: Heliophysics Big Idea 2.2

sources.note: NASA Science heliophysics education page, U.S. government work, public domain. No review date was printed on the page opened 2026-11-26. Supports the intermediate sentence that iron is strongly attracted and copper is not. The broader introductory line is noted as broader, not adopted.
